text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. officer posed as Canadian: Wore Canada's uniform, ordered Somali protester shot, ex-Green Beret captain says.
- Israeli PM, Arafat to meet: Summit to be held in Washington.
- Housing plans threaten Pearson International Airport: Air industry blasts 'greedy developers'.
- Despair, hopelessness fuel Palestinian rage: 'We are so weak, but our weakness is our strength,' human-rights official says.
- Ontario Health Insurance Plan may sue over U.S. scam: Texas lawyer considers offer of contingency fee to recover up to C$85 million.

- Canadian Wheat Board at centre of Prairie storm. After 61 years of relying on the CWB to oversee almost C$6 billion in annual grain sales, some farmers want to break up the marketing monopoly because they think they can get better prices for their crops.
- Silcorp Ltd to buy Becker Milk Co Ltd assets: Takeover target's deal for stores, dairies another roadblock to Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc's hostile bid.
- Ventra bids for rival auto parts maker: Offer highlights consolidation trend.
- Loewen Group acquires another firm: Strategy intact despite Service Corp International bid.
- Market pros foresee a slide in Canadian bonds, U.S. stocks.
- Gasoline price wars take toll on Big Oil. Profit drops expected at Canada's four major integrated oil companies: Imperial Oil Ltd, Petro-Canada, Shell Canada Ltd and Suncor Inc.

- Consumers Distributing Inc's long goodbye almost at an end. The court-appointed receiver of Consumers said it has received no serious bids for the bankrupt retailer and will likely appoint an ouside liquidator next week to sell off the inventory at the chain's remaining 80 stores.
